pageInstruction: Listen to your teacher. Do one part at a time.
pageInstructionReaders: Read each part carefully. Do one part at a time.
sectionLead: Two short paper checks made from this unit's own worksheets. Give Check A before you teach the unit and Check B after it, and you can see what changed. Each part belongs to one lesson.
sectionHonest: This is a classroom check of this unit's lessons. It is not a standardized test, and its points are not a grade.
writingLine: Part {part}: Writing, scored with the guide on the teacher pages ({n} points, 0 to 2 each)
notCovered: Not in the check: {lessons}. Worksheets that cannot be split into single tasks are left out.
formsNote: Printing a check counts as a download, like any worksheet.
teacherPages: Teacher pages: points, class record, and what to do next
teacherNote: The answer keys and the teacher pages come with the paid {plan} plan.
tpHow1: Give Check A before you start the unit and Check B when you finish it. Both checks ask the same kinds of tasks with different numbers, words, and pictures. Before Check A, tell the children that they have not learned these things yet and that it is fine to skip a part.
tpHow2: Read each direction aloud, one part at a time. The check is about what each part asks, not about reading the directions.
tpHow3: Give one point for each task box that is completely right. In a box that says to circle every shape, give the point only when all the right shapes and no others are circled.
tpHow3Plain: Give one point for each task box that is completely right.
tpHow3Writing: Score the writing part with the guide on these pages: 0, 1, or 2 for each point.
tpHonest: This is a classroom check of this unit's lessons. It is not a standardized test. The points show you where to look again; they are not a grade, and they say nothing about a child beyond these tasks.
tpGridLead: Write each child's points for every part, Check A on the left and Check B on the right. After Check B, a part where a child does not have all the points is a part to look at again.
tpNextLead: For each part, go back to the lesson it belongs to. Every worksheet and activity named here is linked on the unit's web page.
tpStillEasier: Teach Lesson {n} again. Then use the easier version of “{title}” for more practice.
tpEasyHarder: Use the harder version of “{title}” as a challenge.
tpEasyOn: No extra practice is needed for this lesson.
tpReadLead: Some parts ask about a short text the children listen to. Read the text aloud twice, then read the direction. The text is not on the children’s page.
hubMetaTitle: K–3 Unit Checks: Before-and-After Checks for Math and Reading
hubMetaDescription: Short printable checks for Kindergarten through Grade 3 units in math and reading. Give one before the unit and one after it, and see what changed.
hubTitle: Unit Checks: Before and After Each Unit
hubLead: A unit check is two short paper checks made from a unit's own worksheets. Give Check A before you teach the unit and Check B after it. Both ask the same kinds of tasks with different numbers, words, and pictures, so you can see what changed.
hubCoverage: Not every unit has a check yet, and a check may leave out a lesson. A worksheet that cannot be split into single tasks is not used.
hubUnitsLink: See every unit and its lesson plans
hubLinkFromUnits: Unit checks: a short check before and after a unit
hubHonest: Each one is a classroom check of a unit's lessons. It is not a standardized test, and its points are not a grade.
wrFullGuide: The full guide with examples is on the teacher pages.
tpWrLead: Give each point 0, 1, or 2: the level whose description matches what you can see in the child’s writing. The examples show what children of this grade write, with their own spelling. Score Check A and Check B the same way.
yearPageMetaTitle: {grade} {subject} Assessments: Beginning, Middle, End of Year
yearPageTitle: {grade} {subject} Assessments: Beginning, Middle, and End of the Year
yearPageLead: Three short paper checks for the school year, made from the worksheets of this grade’s units: one for the beginning, one for the middle, and one for the end of the year. Each part comes from one lesson, so a part a child misses tells you which lesson to go back to.
yearHonest: Each one is a classroom check of our units’ lessons. It is not a standardized test: it does not rank a child against other children, and its points are not a grade. Any line you draw between “ready” and “not yet” is only a guide.
yearLeadEntry_math: An entry check of what a child may already know when school starts: counting, writing numbers, and naming shapes. It checks what a child already knows, not what was taught.
yearLeadEntry_literacy: An entry check of what a child may already know when school starts: letters and beginning sounds. It checks what a child already knows, not what was taught.
yearLead_beginning: What should be secure when a child arrives: the end-of-year skills of {prev}.
yearLead_middle: The units taught by the middle of the year: one part from each of them, and a second part from some.
yearLead_end: The whole year: one part from every unit of the year.
yearFormsUse: Both forms ask the same kinds of tasks with different numbers, words, and pictures. Give Check A; keep Check B for a child who was away or for a second try after you re-teach.
yearTeacherPages: Teacher pages: points, class record, and what to re-teach
yearHubLead: For each grade and subject, a check for the beginning, the middle, and the end of the school year, made from the lessons of the year’s units.
yearHubLink: {grade} {subject}: beginning, middle, and end of the year
yearMeta_K_math: Printable kindergarten math assessments for the beginning, middle, and end of the year: counting, writing numbers to 20, shapes, and taking away within 10.
yearMeta_1_math: Printable first grade math assessments for the beginning, middle, and end of the year: addition and subtraction facts, word problems, tens, and time.
yearMeta_2_math: Printable second grade math assessments for the beginning, middle, and end of the year: three-digit numbers, adding and subtracting, time, and fractions.
yearMeta_3_math: Printable third grade math assessments for the beginning, middle, and end of the year: regrouping, multiplication, area, fractions, and telling time.
yearMeta_K_literacy: Printable kindergarten reading assessments for the beginning, middle, and end of the year: letters and sounds, syllables, first words, and short vowels.
yearMeta_1_literacy: Printable first grade reading and ELA assessments for the beginning, middle, and end of the year: word families, digraphs, silent e, and syllables.
yearMeta_2_literacy: Printable second grade reading and ELA assessments for the beginning, middle, and end of the year: vowel teams, bossy r, verb forms, and synonyms.
yearMeta_3_literacy: Printable third grade reading and ELA assessments for the beginning, middle, and end of the year: syllables, word parts, text evidence, and sentences.
tpYearEyebrow: Check of the year · Teacher pages
tpYearHow_entry: Give this entry check in the first days of school. It checks what a child already knows, not what was taught: nothing in it has been taught yet. Tell the children that it is fine to skip a part.
tpYearHow_beginning: This check asks the end-of-year skills of {prev}: what should be secure when a child arrives. Give it in the first weeks of school.
tpYearHow_middle: This check covers the units taught by the middle of the year. Give it after the last of them.
tpYearHow_end: This check has one part from every unit of the year. Give it in the last weeks of school.
tpYearHonest: This is a classroom check of the lessons of our units. It is not a standardized test. It does not rank a child against other children; the points show you where to look again. They are not a grade, and any line you draw between “ready” and “not yet” is only a guide.
tpYearNextLead: For each part a child misses, go back to the lesson it comes from. The unit’s web page has the lesson’s worksheets, often an easier and a harder version, and practice on screen.
tpYearColNext: If a child misses this part
tpYearGridLead: Write each child’s points for every part of the form you gave, A or B. A part where a child does not have all the points is a part to look at again.
placeHubLead: A short ladder of steps for one skill, across the grades: give the steps in order and stop where the child stops. The step tells you which unit and lesson to start at.
placePageLead: A short ladder of steps in teaching order, each step cut from the lesson that teaches it. Give the steps in order and stop after the first step in which the child misses two tasks, or misses the only task of a one-task step. That step tells you where to start.
placeHonest: This is a classroom placement check. It is not a standardized test: it does not rank a child against other children, and where it stops is a guide to where to start teaching, not a grade.
placeWritingLine: The writing part, for every child apart from the steps: scored with the guide on the teacher pages ({n} points, 0 to 2 each)
placeTeacherPages: Teacher pages: the stop rule, where to start, and a class record
placeStop: Give the steps in order. Stop after the first step in which the child misses two tasks, or misses the only task of a one-task step.
tpPlaceHow: Give the check to one child or a small group. Read each direction aloud. A child who reads well may go on alone; watch where the first mistakes come.
tpPlaceHonest: This is a classroom placement check. It is not a standardized test. It does not rank a child against other children, and the step where a child stops is only a guide to where to start teaching.
tpPlaceColStart: If the child stops here, start at
tpPlaceStartAll: A child who does every step: start at the next unit of the grade, or go on with your plan.
tpPlaceGridLead: One row per child: the form given, the step where the child stopped, and where to start.
placeMetaTitle_counting-number-sense: Math Placement Test: Counting and Number Sense (K–1)
placeMeta_counting-number-sense: A printable math placement test for Kindergarten and Grade 1: counting to 20, missing numbers, comparing numbers, the hundreds chart, and skip counting.
placeMetaTitle_addition-subtraction-fact: Math Placement Test: Addition and Subtraction Facts (K–2)
placeMeta_addition-subtraction-facts: A printable placement test for addition and subtraction facts, Kindergarten to Grade 2: adding, taking away, facts within 10, making ten, and related facts.
placeMeta_place-value: A printable place value placement test for Kindergarten to Grade 3: teen numbers, tens and ones, hundreds, expanded form, comparing, and rounding.
placeMeta_multiplication-facts: A printable multiplication placement test for Grade 3: multiplication as equal groups, the facts for 2 and 5, the missing factor, and multiples of 10.
placeMetaTitle_letters-sounds: Phonics Placement Test: Letters and Sounds (Kindergarten)
placeMeta_letters-sounds: A printable phonics placement test for Kindergarten: finding letters, matching uppercase and lowercase letters, beginning and ending sounds, and short vowels.
placeMetaTitle_blending-decoding: Phonics Placement Test: Blending and Decoding (K–3)
placeMeta_blending-decoding: A printable phonics placement test from Kindergarten to Grade 3: CVC words, sh and ch, silent e, reading vowel teams, syllables, and longer words.
placeMetaTitle_sight-words: Sight Words Placement Test: High-Frequency Words (K–3)
placeMeta_sight-words: A printable sight words placement test from Kindergarten to Grade 3: high-frequency words in sentences and tricky words like said, was, and through.
placeMeta_spelling-patterns: A printable spelling placement test for Grades 1 to 3: short-vowel words, ee and ea, er, ir, and ur, spelling rules, and suffixes like -ful and -less.
placeMeta_sentence-writing: A printable writing placement test from Kindergarten to Grade 3: capital letters, end marks, complete sentences, and a few sentences about a picture.
placeStopOne: In a step of one task, a child who misses it does the matching task of the other form first, and stops only if that task is missed too.
tpPlaceOneTask: One task: if it is missed, give the matching task of the other form before you stop.
tpPlaceWritingAll: Give the writing part to every child, also to a child who stopped earlier on the steps. It is not a step of the ladder: its score places the child in the writing units only (see its guide).
tpPlaceWritingStart: The writing part places a child in the writing units only: use the What next line of each point in its guide.
